thread.title: Apple, Google, Facebook drive down Silicon Valley stocks as Dow plunges 655 points

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Apple, Google, Facebook drive down Silicon Valley stocks as Dow plunges 655 points
text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 2, 2018, 1:50pm PST Updated Feb 2, 2018, 1:54pm PST An index of Silicon Valley’s largest technology stocks fell sharply on Friday as the Dow plunged 655 points. Among the biggest declines on the Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Technology Index were the Valley's most recognizable household names — Google parent Alphabet , Apple and Facebook . All 13 of the stocks on the index posted declines, dragging it down 3.42 percent. The Dow's drop was its worst in more than two years. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) fell 4.43 percent. Investors have been grappling with mixed earnings that saw disappointing iPhone sales and a weak outlook but a promise by the company to return billions of dollars to investors. There was another silver lining hidden in the Cupertino giant's earnings report: While iPhone sales were weak, it’s selling a lot more Apple Watches, Beats headphones and AirPods. All told "other products" sales were up 36 percent year-over-year . Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) also took a big tumble, dropping 5.22 percent on Friday after posting an adjusted fourth-quarter loss the day before as spending soared. The Mountain View company, too, had a silver lining hidden in its earnings: Its cloud services, which it has been growing aggressively to compete with Amazon.com 's (NASDAQ: AMZN) Amazon Web Services , now brings in $1 billion per quarter . Facebook fell 1.48 percent after initially soaring this week on better-than-expected earnings. Almost all of Silicon Valley’s other major tech employers, including Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT), eBay (NASDAQ: EBAY), HP Inc . (NYSE: HPQ), Oracle Corp. (NASDAQ: NASDAQ: ORCL) and Adobe Systems (NASDAQ: ADBE), also fell. All 13 of the stocks on the Bloomberg index declined: Even the best performer on the index, Juniper Networks (NYSE: JNPR), slipped 1.05 percent. One notable exception among Silicon Valley stocks: Viavi Solutions (NASDAQ: VIAV), which jumped 15.34 percent on a big acquisition that analysts applauded. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 2, 2018, 1:50pm PST Updated Feb 2, 2018, 1:54pm PST Related Content
